scope: The vector of orbital occupations is a convex combination of N-element occupation patterns exactly when its entries lie in [0,1] and sum to N. The Lean construction uses the Birkhoff–von Neumann theorem.

Exterior-power amplitudes give basis-independent total Born weight for arbitrary fermion states. For a Slater determinant they give each orbital’s occupation as a sum of squared overlaps with its occupied spin orbitals.

An ensemble of orthonormal Slater determinants realizes its one-particle occupation measurements in every orbital basis. Spectral decomposition relates these expectations to the particle and hole eigenvalues.

Coleman §9, finite spin-orbital basis and trace-N convention. A one-particle density matrix comes from a mixed state of exactly N fermions if and only if its eigenvalues belong to [0,1] and sum to N. Equivalently, the particle and hole matrices are positive semidefinite and the trace is N.
